summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — PYPL +17%, BLK +7%, CBRE +6%, IVZ +5%, BKNG +5%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (PNR -15%, ERIE -12%, DELL -10%, PGR -9%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: PYPL (+17.20%) — Stripe + Advent International (with Block) offered $60.50/share (~$53B) to acquire PayPal, a 28% premium; board meets ~July 20 to weigh it. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — PYPL falls in the fintech/payments-processor category the bot doesn't cover, and this was a one-off M&A gap (89M shares, 446% of avg volume) that pre-market positioning would beat, not a name any technical filter would have screened.

top_movers.catalyst: Stripe + Advent International (with Block) offered $60.50/share (~$53B) to acquire PayPal, a 28% premium; board meets ~July 20 to weigh it.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — PYPL falls in the fintech/payments-processor category the bot doesn't cover, and this was a one-off M&A gap (89M shares, 446% of avg volume) that pre-market positioning would beat, not a name any technical filter would have screened.
top_movers.suggestion: No universe change needed — the stock gapped straight to near the $60.50 deal price, so a momentum/mean-reversion bot chasing it post-announcement has capped upside and poor risk/reward; leave to a dedicated merger-arb strategy if one exists.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS $13.91 vs $12.70 est. and AUM hit record $15.3T; revenue also beat, driving the post-earnings pop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BLK is a mega-cap asset manager trading near $1,000+/share, likely excluded by a price-per-share or financials-sector cap rather than a technical signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gate override that admits universe-excluded names showing a pre-market gap ≥5% on an EPS beat, sized small, rather than relying solely on static price/sector filters.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news; broad rally in rate-sensitive real estate/services names after cooler June CPI (headline -0.4%, core flat) cut Fed hike odds and pulled yields lower.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CBRE sits in large-cap real estate services/management, a sector likely excluded from bot's tradable list since it's neither a core-tech/momentum name nor a classic REIT the strategies track.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rate-sensitive real-estate-services bucket (SIC/GICS 'Real Estate Management') to the universe so CPI-driven yield-sensitive rallies in names like CBRE, JLL, CWK get picked up alongside REITs.

top_movers.catalyst: Barclays raised its IVZ price target to $31 from $26 (Equal Weight) on 7/16, a ~19% target hike ahead of the 7/28 Q2 earnings/AUM print.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IVZ is a mid-cap asset manager (financials/asset-management sector), a category typically excluded from tech/momentum-focused tradable lists; the move was a sell-side target re-rating, not a news/earnings surprise a scanner would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-revision trigger (PT change ≥15% same-day) to the universe screen so financials/asset-managers get pulled in in-day even when the static sector filter would otherwise exclude them.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide travel rally: Jefferies hiked BKNG PT to $190 (from $180) on strong peak-season hotel/flight demand data; peers EXPE and ABNB got similar PT raises the same day — no BKNG-specific news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BKNG is a large-cap travel/consumer-discretionary name whose static universe lists likely predate its April 2026 25-for-1 stock split and were never refreshed to re-include it at its new lower per-share price.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a quarterly universe-refresh job that re-screens eligible tickers by market cap/sector after corporate actions (splits), so recently-split mega-caps like BKNG automatically re-enter tradable universes instead of staying excluded on stale price/ticker metadata.

top_movers.catalyst: Q4 FY26 earnings beat (EPS $1.29 vs $1.24 est, rev $2.91B vs $2.87B est) plus FY27 guidance above consensus; BofA upgraded to Buy, PT raised to $230.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CTAS is a low-beta, low-volatility business-services compounder that typical momentum/mean-reversion scanners exclude via volatility/ATR floors, so it was never a candidate pre-earnings.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-gap override that admits any universe-eligible-by-cap name into a temporary watchlist when it gaps ≥3% on an earnings day, bypassing the low-beta filter for that session only.

top_movers.catalyst: Pentair pre-announced Q2 sales of $930M (vs $1.134B prior guide) and slashed FY26 EPS guidance to $4.60-4.80 on ~$250M pool-channel destocking hit, plus a surprise CFO resignation.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PNR is a ~$10B industrial/water-treatment name, a sector/cap bucket the bot's momentum and news-reactive strategies don't currently cover.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap Industrials (building products/water treatment, $5-20B cap) to the universe scan, or add a pre-earnings 8-K guidance-cut trigger that flags any ticker with a same-day negative preliminary-results filing regardless of universe membership.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news trigger; extension of a multi-week technical breakdown (RSI oversold, sell signal since 2026-07-02) amid slowing premium growth, retention decline to 88%, and Feb-2026 CEO/CFO retirement overhang. Next earnings not until Aug 6.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — ERIE is a mid-cap (~$11-14B), low-float, closely-held P&C insurance holding company, a sector/cap profile the bot's tech/momentum-oriented universe doesn't cover regardless of today's move size.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-agnostic 'accelerating breakdown' scanner (new 52-week low + RSI<30 + volume>1.5x avg) that pulls in non-core-sector mid-caps like insurance/financials for a one-off watchlist add, rather than gating universe membership purely by sector/cap tier.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide AI-hardware selloff (memory pricing/overcapacity fears, CoreWeave hedging reports) plus GF Securities downgrade to Hold after DELL's ~200% run-up.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DELL likely falls outside a large-cap tech/momentum universe scope or was excluded as a richly-valued 'story' name; this was a multi-day sector derate (started 7/15) that a same-day news-reactive or mean-reversion filter wouldn't front-run without pre-market positioning.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-contagion trigger that pulls in peer names (HPE, SMCI, Micron) into the tradable universe once ≥2 of them move >5% on the same news theme within a session.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (reported 7/15): EPS beat estimates ($5.67 vs ~$5.30 est) but combined ratio worsened to ~90% vs ~88.8% est, signaling underwriting margin deterioration; KBW cut price target.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PGR is a large-cap P&C insurer, a sector/name class the bot's momentum and mean-reversion universes don't cover, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the post-earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a financials/insurance earnings-gate that ingests combined-ratio surprise vs. estimate and admits names with post-results gap ≥5% into a next-day mean-reversion or fade watchlist, even if outside the core universe.
